an7.1:1.2: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
an7.1:1.3: There the Buddha addressed the bhikkhus,
an7.1:2.1: “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu with seven qualities is disliked and disapproved by their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.
an7.1:2.3: It’s when a bhikkhu desires material things, honor, and status. They lack conscience and prudence. They have corrupt wishes and wrong view.
an7.1:2.4: A bhikkhu with these seven qualities is disliked and disapproved by their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.
an7.1:3.1: A bhikkhu with seven qualities is liked and approved by their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
an7.1:3.3: It’s when a bhikkhu doesn’t desire material things, honor, and status. They have conscience and prudence. They have few desires and right view.
an7.1:3.4: A bhikkhu with these seven qualities is liked and approved by their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
